items.document: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (Act 43 of 1950), Government of India text as hosted by Tripura High Court
items.quote: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (2), the Election Commission may at any time, for reasons to be recorded, direct a special revision of the electoral roll for any constituency or part of a constituency in such manner as it may think fit:
items.point: The SIR is ordered under this power to revise the roll, which is a different power from the correction and deletion of single entries under section 22.

items.document: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (Act 43 of 1950), Government of India text as hosted by Tripura High Court
items.provision: Section 22, opening words and clause (c) (Correction of entries in electoral rolls); footnote markers omitted
items.quote: If the electoral registration officer for a constituency, on application made to him or on his own motion, is satisfied after such inquiry as he thinks fit, that any entry in the electoral roll of the constituency— ... (c) should be deleted on the ground that the person concerned is dead or has ceased to be ordinarily resident in the constituency or is otherwise not entitled to be registered in that roll, the electoral registration officer shall, subject to such general or special directions, if any, as may be given by the Election Commission in this behalf, amend, transpose or delete the entry after proper verification of facts in such manner as may be prescribed:
items.point: In the Act, deletion is an order by the electoral registration officer removing an entry that is already in the roll, made on an application or on the officer's own motion, on one of three grounds: dead, no longer ordinarily resident, or otherwise not entitled.

items.document: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (Act 43 of 1950), Government of India text as hosted by Tripura High Court
items.quote: Provided that before taking any action on any ground under clause (a) or clause (b) or any action under clause (c) on the ground that the person concerned has ceased to be ordinarily resident in the constituency or that he is otherwise not entitled to be registered in the electoral roll of that constituency, the electoral registration officer shall give the person concerned a reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of the action proposed to be taken in relation to him after proper verification of facts in such manner as may be prescribed.
items.point: Before a deletion for non-residence or ineligibility the person must be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard. The proviso does not name the ground of death.

items.document: Section 22, Representation of the People Act, 1950, Indian Kanoon
items.quote: (c)should be detected on the ground that the person concerned is dead or has ceased to be ordinarily resident in the constituency or is otherwise not entitled to be registered in that roll
items.point: Indian Kanoon's copy prints 'detected' where the government text reads 'deleted'. It is a transcription slip, and the site should quote the government text.

items.document: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (Act 43 of 1950), Government of India text as hosted by Tripura High Court
items.provision: Section 23(1) and 23(2) (Inclusion of names in electoral rolls); footnote markers omitted
items.quote: (1) Any person whose name is not included in the electoral roll of a constituency may apply to the electoral registration officer for the inclusion of his name in that roll. (2) The electoral registration officer shall, if satisfied that the applicant is entitled to be registered in the electoral roll, direct his name to be included therein after proper verification of facts in such manner as may be prescribed:
items.point: The Act's word for a person who is not on a roll is 'not included', and the route back is an application for inclusion.

items.document: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (Act 43 of 1950), Government of India text as hosted by Tripura High Court
items.quote: No amendment, transposition or deletion of any entry shall be made under section 22 and no direction for the inclusion of a name in the electoral roll of a constituency shall be given under this section, after the last date for making nominations for an election in that constituency or in the parliamentary constituency within which that constituency is comprised and before the completion of that election.
items.point: The Act treats deletion under section 22 and inclusion under section 23 as two separate acts.

items.document: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (Act 43 of 1950), Government of India text as hosted by Tripura High Court
items.quote: An appeal shall lie within such time and in such manner as may be prescribed— (a) to the district magistrate or additional district magistrate or executive magistrate or district collector or an officer of equivalent rank, from any order of the electoral registration officer under section 22 or section 23 . (b) to the chief electoral officer, from any order of the district magistrate or the additional district magistrate under clause (a)
items.point: The statutory appeal lies against an order of the electoral registration officer under section 22 or section 23, first to the district magistrate and then to the chief electoral officer.

items.document: Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 (Ministry of Law notification S.O. 2750 of 10 November 1960, as amended), copy hosted by CEO Kerala
items.quote: (2) Every objection to the inclusion of a name in the roll shall be— (a) in Form 7; [and] (b) preferred only by a person whose name is already included in that roll;
items.point: Form 7 is the form for an objection, by an elector of that roll, to a name being in the roll.

items.provision: Form 7 heading (version on Indian Kanoon; the Commission revised the forms in 2022)
items.quote: FORM 7(See rule 13(2) and 26)Application For Objecting Inclusion Or Seeking Deletion Of Name In Electoral Roll
items.point: Form 7 is used both for an objection during a revision (rule 13(2)) and for an application for deletion at other times (rule 26).

items.document: Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 (Ministry of Law notification S.O. 2750 of 10 November 1960, as amended), copy hosted by CEO Kerala
items.quote: 17. Rejection of certain claims and objections.—Any claim or objection which is not lodged within the period, or in the form and manner, herein specified, shall be rejected by the registration officer. 18. Acceptance of claims and objections without inquiry.—If the registration officer is satisfied as to the validity of any claim or objection, he may allow it without further inquiry after the expiry of one week from the date on which it is entered in the list exhibited by him under clause (b) of rule 16: Provided that where before any such claim or objection has been allowed, a demand for inquiry has been made in writing to the registration officer by any person, it shall not be allowed without further inquiry.
items.point: During a revision a Form 7 objection can be rejected for form or time, or allowed after a week on the list if nobody demands an inquiry.

(2) A notice under this rule may be given either personally or by registered post or by affixing it to the person's residence or last known residence within the constituency.
items.point: When a Form 7 objection goes to a hearing, the person objected to must be sent a notice in Form 14.

items.document: Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 (Ministry of Law notification S.O. 2750 of 10 November 1960, as amended), copy hosted by CEO Kerala

(2) At the hearing, the claimant or, as the case may be, the objector and the person objected to and any other person who, in the opinion of the registration officer, is likely to be of assistance to him, shall be entitled to appear and be heard.
items.point: The person objected to is entitled to appear and be heard, and the officer must record a decision.

items.document: Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 (Ministry of Law notification S.O. 2750 of 10 November 1960, as amended), copy hosted by CEO Kerala
items.quote: If it appears to the registration officer that owing to inadvertence or error during preparation, the names of any electors have been left out of the roll and that remedial action should be taken under this rule, the registration officer shall— (a) prepare a list of the names and other details of such electors;
items.point: The Rules' own phrase for names missing from a roll being prepared is 'left out of the roll', with a separate rule for putting them back.

items.document: Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 (Ministry of Law notification S.O. 2750 of 10 November 1960, as amended), copy hosted by CEO Kerala
items.provision: Rule 21A (Deletion of names), substituted by S.O. 814(E) of 3 September 1987
items.quote: 21A. Deletion of names.—If it appears to the registration officer at any time before the final publication of the roll that owing to inadvertence or error or otherwise, the names of dead persons or of persons who have ceased to be, or are not, ordinarily residents in the constituency or of persons who are otherwise not entitled to be registered in that roll, have been included in the roll and that remedial action should be taken under this rule, the registration officer, shall— (a) prepare a list of the names and other details of such electors; (b) exhibit on the notice board of his office a copy of the list together with a notice as to the time and place at which the question of deletion of these names from the roll will be considered, and also publish the list and the notice in such other manner as he may think fit; and (c) after considering any verbal or written objections that may be preferred, decide whether all or any of the names should be deleted from the roll: Provided that before taking any action under this rule in respect of any person on the ground that he has ceased to be, or is not, ordinarily resident in the constituency, or is otherwise not entitled to be registered in that roll, the registration officer shall make every endeavour to give him a reasonable opportunity to show cause why the action proposed should not be taken in relation to him.
items.point: During a revision, before final publication, the officer can delete names that 'have been included in the roll' only after publishing a list and a notice, considering objections, and, for non-residence or ineligibility, giving a chance to show cause. It needs no Form 7.

items.document: Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 (Ministry of Law notification S.O. 2750 of 10 November 1960, as amended), copy hosted by CEO Kerala
items.quote: (a) prepare a list of amendments to carry out his decisions under rules 18, 20, [21 and 21A] and to correct any clerical or printing errors or other inaccuracies subsequently discovered in the roll;
items.point: Decisions on objections (rules 18 and 20) and deletions under rule 21A take effect at final publication.

items.document: Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 (Ministry of Law notification S.O. 2750 of 10 November 1960, as amended), copy hosted by CEO Kerala
items.provision: Rule 23(1) (Appeals from orders deciding claims and objections)
items.quote: An appeal shall lie from any decision of the registration officer under rule 20, [rule 21 or rule 21A] to such officer of Government as the Election Commission may designate in this behalf (hereinafter referred to as the appellate officer): Provided that an appeal shall not lie where the person desiring to appeal has not availed himself of his right to be heard by, or to make representations to, the registration officer on the matter which is the subject of appeal.
items.point: During a revision, decisions on objections and on deletions under rule 21A are appealable, but only by someone who used the chance to be heard first.

items.document: Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 (Ministry of Law notification S.O. 2750 of 10 November 1960, as amended), copy hosted by CEO Kerala
items.quote: Where the roll or any part thereof is to be revised intensively in any year, it shall be prepared afresh and rules 4 to 23 shall apply in relation to such revision as they apply in relation to the first preparation of a roll.
items.point: In an intensive revision the roll is 'prepared afresh', and the claims, objections and rule 21A procedure (rules 4 to 23) apply to it.

If the appellant remains unsatisfied, a second appeal may be preferred before the Chief Electoral Officer within 30 days of the DM’s order, as per Section 24(b) of the RP Act, 1950 read with Rule 27 of the RER, 1960.

Having considered the rival submissions, the issue that arises for our consideration is whether the procedure adopted under the Impugned SIR while removing the name of electors is in derogation of the safeguards embodied in Rule 21A of 1960 Rules.
items.point: The Court tested the whole SIR removal, unreturned forms included, against Rule 21A, the deletion rule.

items.document: Supreme Court of India, Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India & Ors., W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected matters, judgment, 2026 INSC 564 (Surya Kant CJI and Joymalya Bagchi J.)
items.quote: Paragraph 4(b) of the Guidelines provides that the draft roll shall include the names of all electors who have submitted their Enumeration Forms, while those in respect of whom forms have not been received are not included at this stage. It is of significance that such non-inclusion is not tantamount to a final deletion, but is only a provisional step, preceding the statutory process of claims and objections.
items.point: The Court held that leaving a name off the draft is a provisional step and not a final deletion.

items.document: Supreme Court of India, Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India & Ors., W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected matters, judgment, 2026 INSC 564 (Surya Kant CJI and Joymalya Bagchi J.)
items.quote: 139. Finally, the Guidelines under Paragraph 11 (d) clarify that exclusion from the final electoral roll occurs only after completion of the scrutiny process, including enquiry and opportunity of hearing, and that such electors retain the right to challenge the decision. This makes it clear that the operative act of deletion is preceded by due process, consistent with the mandate of Rule 21A of the 1960 Rules. ... 141. In particular, what Rule 21A of the 1960 Rules contemplates as a singular, event-specific exercise of deletion is, under the SIR framework, distributed across multiple procedural stages, beginning with enumeration, followed by draft publication, and culminating in the claims and objections process.
items.point: The Court treats the SIR as a deletion process spread over stages, beginning with enumeration, and places 'the operative act of deletion' at the end, after the hearing.

items.document: Supreme Court of India, Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India & Ors., W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected matters, judgment, 2026 INSC 564 (Surya Kant CJI and Joymalya Bagchi J.)
items.quote: Equally, the contention that non-inclusion in the draft roll results in automatic or final deletion cannot be accepted. The draft roll is, by design, provisional. It triggers a participatory process in which electors are afforded an opportunity to assert their entitlement, produce supporting material, and contest any proposed exclusion. The finality attaches only after this process is complete, and after compliance with the safeguards of notice, enquiry, and hearing.
items.point: The Court rejected the argument that leaving a name off the draft is itself a deletion.

items.document: Supreme Court of India, Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India & Ors., W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected matters, judgment, 2026 INSC 564 (Surya Kant CJI and Joymalya Bagchi J.)
items.quote: We are, therefore, of the considered view that the deletions effected pursuant to the Impugned Special Intensive Revision cannot be said to be contrary to the procedure prescribed under Rule 21A of the 1960 Rules. The safeguards of notice and hearing are preserved in substance, and the process adopted by the Commission remains within the bounds of the statutory mandate.
items.point: The Court calls what the SIR produced 'deletions' and holds they comply in substance with Rule 21A.

items.document: Supreme Court of India, Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India & Ors., W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected matters, judgment, 2026 INSC 564 (Surya Kant CJI and Joymalya Bagchi J.)
items.quote: d) The deletions effected pursuant to the Impugned SIR exercise cannot be said to be contrary to the procedure prescribed under Rule 21A of the 1960 Rules. The safeguards of notice and hearing are preserved in substance, and the process adopted by the Commission remains within the bounds of the statutory mandate.
items.point: The operative conclusion repeats 'deletions'.

items.document: Supreme Court of India, Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India & Ors., W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected matters, judgment, 2026 INSC 564 (Surya Kant CJI and Joymalya Bagchi J.)
items.quote: In addition thereto, all persons who are domiciled in Bihar and whose names have been erroneously deleted on the ground that they are absent, dead, shifted or in duplication may assail the decision of the Commission by way of judicial review.
items.point: For the absent, dead, shifted and duplicate category, which is how the 65 lakh not on the draft were labelled, the Court's final order says 'deleted'.

items.document: PTI report on rediff.com, 'Absence from draft SIR doesn't mean deletion of name, ECI tells HC' (press report of argument before the Bombay High Court at Goa, not a document of the Commission)
items.provision: Report of submissions by the Commission's counsel
items.quote: "Absence from the draft SIR roll does not automatically amount to deletion," said Advocate Kumbhakoni. As the roll is being prepared afresh, a name missing from the draft roll has not technically been 'deleted', he said.
items.point: As reported, the Commission argued in court in October 2026 that a name missing from an SIR draft has not been deleted, because the roll is prepared afresh.

answers.a: Not at the draft stage. In the Act and the Rules, deletion is an order of the electoral registration officer removing an entry already in the roll: under section 22(c) on an application (Form 7, rule 26) or on the officer's own motion, and during a revision under rule 21A, or on a Form 7 objection decided under rules 17 to 20. Form 7 is one way to start a deletion, not the only one, since section 22 and rule 21A also let the officer act on his own motion. The SIR orders say that electors whose enumeration forms were not returned 'can not be included' or 'will not be included in the draft roll', and the Commission's own lists call this 'non-inclusion'. The Supreme Court held on 27 May 2026 (para 134 and 142) that this 'non-inclusion is not tantamount to a final deletion, but is only a provisional step'. So the plain legal description of the roughly 65 lakh in Bihar at the draft is 'not included in the draft roll'. The same judgment, however, treats the whole SIR as a deletion process spread over stages (para 141) and calls the outcome 'deletions' (para 144 and 186(d)), including for those marked absent, dead, shifted or duplicate (para 186(h)). Once the final roll is published without them, the Court's own word is 'deleted'.
answers.b: Names not carried into the draft: no individual notice, hearing or order before the draft. The lists of these names, with the BLO's 'probable reasons', are published (letter of 27.10.2025 para 2(a); Supreme Court order of 14.08.2025 para 3). The elector's remedy is a claim for inclusion in Form 6 with the declaration during the claims period (Guidelines para 4(c); order of 14.08.2025 para 3(vii)). Names on the draft that are then removed, whether on a Form 7 objection or on the officer's own enquiry: an inquiry and a fair and reasonable opportunity (order of 24.06.2025 para 14), a hearing and a written or speaking order (PIB 01.08.2025; Guidelines para 5 and 11(d)), and appeal to the District Magistrate under section 24(a), then to the Chief Electoral Officer under section 24(b) (order para 14). Under the Rules, a Form 7 objection during a revision needs notice to the person objected to in Form 14 and a summary inquiry where they can be heard (rules 19 and 20), and appeal under rule 23. A deletion on the officer's own motion before final publication needs a published list and notice, consideration of objections, and a chance to show cause for non-residence or ineligibility (rule 21A). Outside a revision, a deletion under section 22 needs a hearing for non-residence or ineligibility (section 22 proviso, which does not cover death) and is appealable under section 24. The Supreme Court held that the SIR's distributed procedure satisfies Rule 21A in substance (para 140 to 144).
answers.c: Yes, both blur it in places. The Commission's orders keep the words apart: 'not included in the draft roll' and 'non-inclusion' for unreturned forms, and 'delete any entry from the draft roll' only for names that appeared in the draft (order of 24.06.2025 para 13 and 14; letter of 27.10.2025 para 2(a)). But its press release of 30.09.2025 uses one word for both, 'Total Electors removed from Draft List 65 lakhs' and 'Ineligible Electors removed from draft list 3.66 lakhs'. In October 2026 its counsel told the Bombay High Court, as PTI reported, that absence from the draft is not deletion. The Supreme Court's order of 14.08.2025 says 'not included' and 'non-inclusion'. Its judgment of 27.05.2026 uses 'excluded from the draft roll' (para 10.9, 10.10, 137) and holds non-inclusion is not a final deletion (para 134, 142). But it also frames the issue as 'removal of names' tested against Rule 21A (heading E.3.2, para 129), describes the SIR as Rule 21A's 'exercise of deletion' distributed across stages beginning with enumeration (para 141), and in its operative conclusions calls the results 'deletions' (para 144, 186(d)) and speaks of names 'erroneously deleted on the ground that they are absent, dead, shifted or in duplication' (para 186(h)). The site can say 'not included in the draft' or 'left off the draft' for the draft stage with the orders' and the Court's support, and 'excluded' is the Court's own word. It should not say the authorities never call these deletions: the Supreme Court does, for the final outcome.
